label: SwiftUI
summary: SwiftUI views composed from stacks and modifiers. Layout is stack-based; sizes are points. Design tokens live in one Theme type or the asset catalog, so a token is used by name and follows the appearance.

elements.frame: A VStack for a column, an HStack for a row, a ZStack when children overlap, a LazyVGrid for a grid. A frame with a background or border applies those as modifiers.
elements.group: A Group, or the children directly.
elements.text: A Text with .font, .fontWeight, .lineSpacing and .tracking from the text style.
elements.image: An Image (AsyncImage for a remote one) with .resizable() and .scaledToFill() or .scaledToFit().
elements.icon: An Image(systemName:) for the closest SF Symbol, or the project's icon asset of the same name.
elements.vector: A Shape with the path data from the spec, or an image asset.
elements.rect: A RoundedRectangle or Rectangle filled with the paint.
elements.ellipse: A Circle or Ellipse filled with the paint.
elements.instance: The project's view of the same name, with the instance's props as initializer arguments.

layout.grid: LazyVGrid with the frame's columns as GridItem(.flexible()).
layout.none: ZStack(alignment: .topLeading); children with an absolute position use .offset(x:y:) from x and y.
layout.padding: .padding(N) for all sides, .padding(.vertical, N) and .padding(.horizontal, N) for two values, .padding(.top, N) and the others for four.
layout.justify: Spacer() between children for space-between; the stack's alignment for start, center and end along its axis.
layout.align: The stack's alignment parameter: .leading, .center, .trailing for a VStack; .top, .center, .bottom for an HStack.
layout.hug: No frame modifier; the content decides (.fixedSize() when the parent would stretch it).

tokens.reference: Use the token by name (Theme.color.primary, or Color("color/primary") from the asset catalog), never write the value in a view.
tokens.naming: A token name's slashes become nested members: color/primary is Theme.color.primary, space/4 is Theme.space.s4.
tokens.modes: Theme values such as Dark are the asset catalog's appearance variants. Never branch on colorScheme in a view for a token.

components: One View per component in the spec, with its props as initializer arguments and its variants as an enum parameter. An instance is that view with the instance's props, not a copy of its layers.
rules: Follow the spec's sizes and spacing exactly; they are points.
Order modifiers the way SwiftUI applies them: padding before background, background before clipShape.
Use theme tokens for every color, spacing and radius the spec names a token for.
Support Dynamic Type for text unless the spec fixes a size on purpose.
A layer with notes in the spec carries instructions from the designer; follow them.
